label: AI Bubble Economy
title: The AI Bubble Economy: What Happens When the Money Doesn't Add Up
body:
An economic bubble forms when asset prices climb far beyond what future profits could justify. Major tech companies are spending over $700 billion on AI infrastructure in 2026 alone, while revenue from AI products lags far behind. Some analysts estimate the industry would need to generate roughly $650 billion in new annual revenue just to earn modest returns on current infrastructure spending—a gap that raises real concerns about sustainability.

The mechanism works like this: companies borrow and spend heavily building data centres and buying chips, hoping future AI revenue will justify the cost. When investment outpaces actual demand, asset values can correct sharply—triggering layoffs, tightening credit, and spilling into the wider economy. Meanwhile, some AI firms use circular financing, investing in each other's services, which can mask weak underlying demand.

For ordinary people, the stakes are real. Retirement funds hold significant AI-related stock. If valuations drop, pension portfolios suffer. Companies that overspent on AI may cut non-tech staff to save money. And recessions can actually accelerate automation, as struggling businesses adopt cost-cutting technology—meaning workers could lose jobs even as investors lose money.
